extraction_notes.note: Written as \begin{definition} but each body is 'Find, if possible, ... such that' a design problem; typed problem rather than definition.

The regulator equations (same \label III09) are pasted verbatim into Lemma 3, Theorem 1 and Theorem 2; each copy is an environment fact so each got an equation node, and \eqref{III09} resolves to the first. Definition 2 is titled 'Error feedback' but Theorem 2 calls it the 'output feedback' problem; treated as the same problem.
One sentence defines several symbols (consensus rate, contract rate, transition matrix; and Mf plus the mean-value identity); whole-sentence rule kept them as one node each.
Assumptions are \item entries of a list; spans start after the [A1)]-style item label (A5 includes its lead-in sentence).
Introduction literature survey, motivational paragraph opening Section 3.1, and the conclusion's future-work sentence (error feedback extension) were not made nodes.
